A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DETR-ViP paper, including complete Appendices A–F. Pages 2–23 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance. Page 1 differs only in author affiliations and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original DETR-ViP benchmark results and component ablations in Section 4, plus transfer experiments, sensitivity studies, and visual-prompt analyses in Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, and appendix experiments unchanged. The paper reports its own empirical outcomes alongside results attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix D retain the same architecture, global prompt integration, visual-textual relation distillation, and selective fusion. Algorithm steps, objectives, and inference procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Objects365 V1 and GoldG and evaluate on COCO, LVIS, ODinW, and Roboflow100. Visual-G, Visual-I, and all appendix task and scenario coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same T-Rex2 and YOLOE variants, and Table 2 retains the same T-Rex2 comparators. Comparator membership in the ablations and appendix comparisons is also identical.

E3.justification: Model configurations, prompt-sampling procedures, evaluation metrics, and experimental settings are identical. Appendix E retains the same 12-epoch downstream-transfer experiment with all modules except the replacement classification layer frozen.

E4.justification: The component ablations, transfer and loss comparisons, hyperparameter studies, prompt-count and chunk-size sensitivity analyses, and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout Section 4.4 and Appendices E–F.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical throughout the main text and appendices. No run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 reports DETR-ViP-T at 43.2 COCO AP and 41.1 LVIS AP in both versions. The remaining tables and appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(12), including the loss formulations, selective-fusion gating, and IISR definition, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about visual-prompt discriminability, the proposed components, and detection performance. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are identical. Appendix B retains the limitation that visual prompts lack the explicit attribute and spatial descriptions available through text, with no revised applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A, D, and E retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, and resource-release commitment. The project-page URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix C, and the reference list are identical. No cited works or positioning relative to earlier detection and contrastive-learning approaches are added, removed, or revised.

P1.justification: Page 1 revises author affiliations and superscripts: Bo Qian and Xing Wei gain the State Key Laboratory affiliation, while Bo Qian's listed Hikrobot affiliation is removed. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page affiliation block is rearranged, placing CCAI and Hikrobot together beneath the added laboratory line, and the marginal arXiv stamp is updated. All figures, tables, captions, and subsequent page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision changes affiliation information and its presentation but leaves the methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged, including all appendices. These limited front-matter edits produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
